answer: A first answer needs 2 co-signatures from established identities, each of which shares liability for the newcomer's verdict. Since the trellis liability is published with the signature, the shale audit shows who vouched, and self-sponsorship costs more than it saves. A farm has to recruit that support from outside its own cluster, because an internal co-signature is flagged on the beacon graph and the sponsor's bond is exposed. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
